name: Yurii Can Do Everything
description: Yurii is sure he can do everything. Can he solve this task, though? He has an array $$$a$$$ consisting of $$$n$$$ positive integers. Let's call a subarray $$$a[l...r]$$$ good if the following conditions are simultaneously satisfied: $$$l+1 \leq r-1$$$, i. e. the subarray has length at least $$$3$$$; $$$(a_l \oplus a_r) = (a_{l+1}+a_{l+2}+\ldots+a_{r-2}+a_{r-1})$$$, where $$$\oplus$$$ denotes the bitwise XOR operation . In other words, a subarray is good if the bitwise XOR of the two border elements is equal to the sum of the rest of the elements. Yurii wants to calculate the total number of good subarrays. What is it equal to? An array $$$c$$$ is a subarray of an array $$$d$$$ if $$$c$$$ can be obtained from $$$d$$$ by deletion of several (possibly, zero or all) elements from the beginning and several (possibly, zero or all) elements from the end.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$3 \leq n \leq 2\cdot 10^5$$$) — the length of $$$a$$$. The second line contains $$$n$$$ integers $$$a_1,a_2,\ldots,a_n$$$ ($$$1 \leq a_i \lt 2^{30}$$$) — elements of $$$a$$$.
output_specification: Output a single integer — the number of good subarrays.
approach_summary: Exploit monotonicity of two-pointer invariant [L, R]. Advance R while shifting L forward to maintain validity, running in O(N) amortized time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1438E — Yurii Can Do Everything [34. Two Pointers]
topic_editorial.key_invariant: When scanning contiguous subarrays or paired indices, advancing the right pointer $R$ monotonically tightens or relaxes the constraint, allowing the left pointer $L$ to only advance forward without ever needing to reset backwards.
